Absolute certainty in empirical science is a mirage, impossible because science relies on inductive reasoning. We can observe a million white swans, but we cannot logically prove a black one does not exist. Our current theories are merely the best available models, forever vulnerable to falsification by tomorrow's anomalies.

Yet, this inherent uncertainty is precisely what makes science our most reliable path to knowledge. It is a self-correcting map, not a dogma. Religion builds castles on perceived bedrock; science builds ships to navigate an ocean of doubt. By constantly testing its hull against the waves of reality, science ensures that even if we never reach the shores of absolute truth, we are always sailing in the right direction.
